attempts.raw_response: The cuff will tighten around your arm as it inflates, which is normal. You'll feel pressure, but it shouldn't be painful. The display will show your systolic and diastolic readings along with your pulse rate. Most devices categorize results using color codes or indicators—green for normal, yellow for elevated, and red for high blood pressure. Some models save readings automatically to your profile, while others may require you to confirm saving. If your readings are consistently high or outside your normal range, consult your healthcare provider. It's recommended to take multiple readings at different times of day for the most accurate picture of your blood pressure.

pair.human_continuation: Also, try to avoid talking, as that can affect your reading. Your blood pressure and pulse will flash on the screen when the cuff is done taking your reading. Leave the cuff in place, and wait 1-2 minutes. Take a second reading using the same techniques, then average the 2 readings if they're close. If the readings are not close, take a third reading, and then average all 3. Your blood pressure will increase momentarily after each reading, so you need to allow a little time to let your true blood pressure recover. If you get a high reading, take a deep breath. Wait 5 minutes or so, and try again to see if you get a lower reading.
pair.prefix: You'll find a power button or a switch to activate the power. Sometimes, the "Power" button is the same as the "Start" button. Pressing it once turns it on, while pressing it again activates the measurement process. If the device tracks multiple users, make sure to select your profile. Once you are set, the "Start" or "Go" button will start the blood pressure reading process. Do not move while the cuff inflates and deflates, reading your blood pressure.
